title: How to plan for retirement using FIRE (Financial Independence, Retire Early)
description: The math of quitting the rat race in your 30s or 40s using the '4% Rule'.
content:
The standard American retirement plan is: Work until 65, save 10%, and hope Social Security exists. The FIRE movement (Financial Independence, Retire Early) challenges this script. FIRE is not about eating ramen noodles forever; it is about aggressive front-loading of savings so that work becomes optional decades early. By saving 50-70% of your income for 10-15 years, you can mathematically reach a 'Crossover Point' where your investment income exceeds your expenses. This guide explains the core formulas behind early freedom.

Key Takeaways

  • The 25x Rule: You need to save 25 times your annual expenses to retire. If you spend $40,000/year, your FIRE number is $1 Million.
  • The 4% Rule: Studies show you can safely withdraw 4% of your portfolio in year 1 (adjusted for inflation thereafter) and have a 95% chance of never running out of money over 30 years.
  • Savings Rate is Speed: Your income doesn't determine retirement date; your savings rate does. A 50% savings rate means for every 1 year you work, you buy 1 year of freedom.
  • Healthcare is the Hurdle: Retiring before 65 means you don't have Medicare. You must budget for ACA (Obamacare) premiums.

Why It Matters (US Context)

The US is uniquely suited for FIRE due to high professional salaries and low-cost market access. However, the cost of healthcare is the primary risk factor. Understanding how to manage your Adjusted Gross Income (AGI) to qualify for ACA subsidies is a critical skill for early retirees.

The Varieties of FIRE

FIRE isn't one-size-fits-all. Pick your flavor.

1. LeanFIRE (The Minimalist)

  • Expenses: <$40k/year.
  • Target: <$1 Million.
  • Lifestyle: Frugal, paid-off house, cooking at home, low-cost hobbies. Fastest path to exit the workforce.

2. FatFIRE (The High Roller)

  • Expenses: >$100k/year.
  • Target: >$2.5 Million.
  • Lifestyle: Travel, dining out, new cars. Requires a high income and longer career to achieve.

3. BaristaFIRE / CoastFIRE

You save enough (e.g., $500k) that compound interest will hit your retirement number by age 65 without adding another dime. You then quit your stressful corporate job and work a low-stress job (Barista) just to cover daily bills and health insurance.

The Execution Plan

  1. Calculate Your Gap: Income - Expenses. Maximize this gap. It is easier to cut expenses by $10k than to earn $10k more (due to taxes).
  2. Build the 'Bridge': You can't touch 401(k) money easily before 59.5. You need a 'Bridge Account' (Taxable Brokerage) with 5 years of expenses to tide you over until you can access retirement funds (using a Roth Conversion Ladder).
  3. Invest Aggressively: 100% VTI/VOO. You need growth to sustain a 40-50 year retirement. Bonds are risky because they might not beat inflation long-term.
  4. Geo-Arbitrage: Consider moving from a HCOL city (NY/SF) to a LCOL area (Midwest/Portugal) once you retire. This instantly drops your 'FIRE Number' by 30-50%.

Frequently Asked Questions

What about the 10% penalty for early withdrawal?

There are ways around it. The 'Rule of 55', 'SEPP 72(t)', and 'Roth Conversion Ladder' allow you to access retirement funds early penalty-free. Do not let the 59.5 age limit scare you.

Is the 4% rule safe for 50 years?

The Trinity Study only looked at 30 years. For a 50-year retirement, many experts suggest a safer withdrawal rate of 3.25% or 3.5%. This requires a larger portfolio (30x expenses).

What do I do all day?

The 'Retire To' problem. You need a purpose. Volunteering, hobbies, part-time passion work. FIRE is about 'Financial Independence', not necessarily sitting on a couch doing nothing.
